general_conventions: Mark categories follow OCR's 'MACB' scheme: B = independent mark for a point that must be explicitly seen; M = method mark on which later A marks depend (no M, no dependent A); C = compensatory method mark that can be inferred from correct later working even if the equation is not written; A = accuracy/answer mark depending on an M or C mark.

Annotations: DO NOT ALLOW = not creditworthy; IGNORE = irrelevant material, neither credited nor penalised; ALLOW = acceptable alternative; words in brackets are not essential; underlined words must appear; ECF = error carried forward from an earlier part; AW = alternative wording accepted; ORA = reverse argument accepted.

Significant figures: if data are given to 2 s.f., answers to 2 or more s.f. are accepted; an answer to fewer than 2 s.f. is penalised once only across the whole paper unless the guidance says otherwise.
Crossed-out work is not marked if an alternative is offered; NR is used for no response; 0 is awarded for an attempt with no credit (e.g. copying the question).
Section A (20 MCQs, 1 mark each) is marked by the letter alone; Section B is structured questions totalling 50 marks.
Units shown in brackets in the answer column are not required for the mark when the unit is printed on the answer line.

questions.context: % uncertainty in density from mass and radius uncertainties
marking_points: B1: correct option D (6% from mass + 3×5% from radius cubed)
pitfalls: forgetting to triple the radius % uncertainty (gives 11%)

questions.context: tension in rope lifting 7.0 kg mass accelerating upward at 2.0 m s^-2
marking_points: B1: correct option D (T = m(g + a))
pitfalls: using T = ma only (14 N) or mg − ma (55 N)

questions.context: true statements about forces on a floating cork
marking_points: B1: correct option D (floating: weight equals upthrust; net force is zero and upthrust equals weight (not mass) of water displaced)
pitfalls: confusing mass with weight of fluid displaced

questions.context: force constant of spring compressed from 5.0 cm to 4.0 cm by forces in diagram
marking_points: B1: correct option C (k = F/x with x = 1.0 cm = 0.010 m)
pitfalls: not converting cm to m
diagram force values not readable in text extraction

questions.context: which inequality holds for a balloon accelerating downward with upthrust, weight and drag
marking_points: B1: correct option D (downward acceleration needs weight to exceed sum of upward forces)
pitfalls: treating air resistance as downward when moving down

questions.context: maximum pressure of a brick on a table

questions.context: why bright and dark fringes form with two slits
